analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md: the 'Last updated' date moves to 2026-10-28, and head lines 531-550 add a paragraph on SSD eviction, namely SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest, SSDBlockIndex.oldest and oldestFirstSnapshot (a binary-heap LRU snapshot). No executable code, configuration, keys or protocol messages change, so no security control is altered in this diff. The new text is consistent with the T-041 posture: file leases, epoch validation and the removal lock still govern retirement, eviction keeps the model's cache epoch, and KEK wipe remains the cryptographic purge. It does not alter the TTL (30 minutes), the HMAC lookup tags, the salt scoping, or the SEC-035 accepted risk. The text says a closed store refuses removals and the eviction pass ends at the first attempt that frees nothing. It also says other refusals, such as an unsafe root or an unreadable epoch record, let the pass continue. This is a descriptive claim about unchanged or separately changed source. SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.swift is not in this batch, so I could not verify it. Whether the described behavior matches that implementation is an integration question for the code PR, not a doc regression. The documented eviction order (last hit, then lexicographic tag) is not a new at-rest disclosure, because the tags are already HMAC-keyed. The remaining 2026-10-24 to 2026-10-28 text is context only. No new attack surface, invalidated assumption or threat-model gap was identified from this doc-only change.
